page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Provisioned on the KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, the server features 2 vCPUs running on 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. Architectural hardware extensions include AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no local NVMe storage.

Performance testing reflects high single-threaded processing metrics relative to multi-core throughput. The instance achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 3059.78 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1939.0, both categorized in the top performance quartile. Multi-core operations scale linearly with core availability, registering a stress-ng multi-core score of 3062.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2433.0. Potentially uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 37.76 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 2.79 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM capacity renders the instance specialized for compute-focused tasks requiring minimal memory footprints. Lack of local disk storage requires reliance on network-attached storage volumes for stateful applications. The server offers efficiency for single-threaded processing, lightweight web microservices, compilation scripts, and basic utility workloads.

Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and no local disk storage is included. Hardware benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1939.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3059.78. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance, this instance profile offers cost-effective execution for single-threaded processing tasks, small background workers, utility scripts, and low-density application microservices.
